text:
The abstract describes a review that surveys theoretical models of dust production (supernovae, AGB stars, ISM processing, other stellar sources, and quasar winds) and recent observational findings at high redshift. Its central focus is on identifying and evaluating the origins and evolution of dust in the early universe, rather than on spatial offsets between far‑infrared and ultraviolet emission as a marker of separate star‑formation phases. The candidate hypothesis about FIR–UV separation and simultaneous obscured/unobscured star formation is not presented as a primary hypothesis of the study; it is outside the scope of the review’s stated aims.

VERDICT: REJECT
